question: Why are German pretzels dipped in a lye bath before baking?
answer: Because alkali speeds the Maillard reaction. In neutral dough many amino groups carry an extra proton and react slowly; a dip in dilute sodium hydroxide strips it off, so surface sugars and proteins combine far faster. In the oven the lye reacts with carbon dioxide and turns harmless, leaving a mahogany skin.
move: Change the conditions and the same ingredients can react many times faster.
reference: Hodge, Chemistry of browning reactions in model systems, Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry, 1953
